translations.text: Then Ananias came to the chosen champion and laid his hands on him with this greeting: "Saul, my brother, the Saviour, who spoke to you on the way, has sent me to you,
They were greatly astonished and said, "Why, is this not the cruel persecutor of Christian men? How is it that he preaches the faith of Christ?"
Afterwards, after some time, a call came from the Holy Spirit to the faithful company, saying, "Send Paul and Barnabas to the work for which I have chosen them."
Then the holy company, at God's command and by his choice, sent them out to teach all peoples about Christ's coming for the redemption of the world."
"Barnabas was then Paul's companion in the preaching for a long time. Then at last they thought it best to go their separate ways, and so they did.
as the Jews did. Rather, he was a spokesman and defender of the old law, with great steadfastness: he thought that the faith of Christ was opposed to the old ordinance.
But the Saviour, who established the old law with various figures, was the same who later, when he was present, turned them into truth according to their spiritual meaning.
God Almighty, who knows all things, saw his intention: that he did not persecute faithful men out of malice,

because he is the head of Christian men, and he grieves over whatever his limbs suffer on earth, as he said through his prophet: "Whoever touches you, it will be as painful to me as if he touched the pupil of my eye."
He remained without sight for three days, because he had denied Christ's resurrection on the third day.
He baptised the wolf and made him into a lamb. He changed his name along with his ways, and he who had earlier afflicted God's church with fierce persecution was then its true herald.
He was often in great danger, both at sea and on land, in the wilderness, among robbers, in hunger and in thirst, and in many vigils, in cold and in nakedness, and in many prisons.
He hurried on with his preaching as if he wanted to bring all mankind to God's kingdom: with teaching, with prayers and with letters, he always urged people toward God's will.
His teachings and his way of life are beyond our understanding, but blessed is he who diligently obeys his exhortations.
Peter left behind little things, a bag and a net, but he left behind all things when, for the love of God, he would have nothing.
He said, "We follow you." It is not perfect to give up many possessions unless one follows God.
The Saviour answered, "Truly I tell you, you who follow me shall sit on twelve judgment seats in the regeneration, when I sit on the throne of my majesty;
and then you will judge the twelve tribes of Israel." By "regeneration" he meant the general resurrection, in which our bodies will be regenerated to incorruption, that is, to eternal things.
The third birth will be at the general resurrection, in which our bodies will be born again as incorruptible bodies.
and this number has a greater meaning than the unlearned can understand. So this twelvefold number signifies the whole circle of the world.
The apostles and all the chosen who followed their example will be judges with Christ on the great day.
The first company is that of the apostles and those who follow their example, who gave up all worldly things for God's name. They will be the judges, and no judgment will be passed on them.
The second order is that of faithful laypeople. Judgment is appointed for them, such that they will be separated from the fellowship of the rejected,
as the Lord says: "Come to me, you blessed of my Father, and receive the kingdom that has been prepared for you from the beginning of the world."
One order is that of the rejected who had knowledge of God, but did not practise their faith by keeping God's commandments. These will be condemned.
The other order is that of the heathens, who had no knowledge of God. In them the apostle's saying is fulfilled: "Those who sinned without God's law will also perish without any law."
Whoever lives among monks and deceitfully cheats the monastery of its possessions is the companion of Judas, who betrayed Christ, and he will receive his punishment with the inhabitants of hell.
The prophet said: "I saw, through God's Spirit, when the nobleman got down from his chariot and went to meet you, and you took his payments in money and in clothing.
